transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep getting these awful doubts that I’ve missed something important. It might be a number on the mortgage payment, something in a client proof, or whether I latched the door. Even if I know I checked it, the thought comes right back—like, what if this is the mistake that costs me everything?
When that doubt hits, do you find yourself checking or rechecking to feel sure?

Yes. I’ll reopen files and reread emails over and over, or check the payment confirmation again. Sometimes I silently repeat the figures in my head until they feel settled. A simple invoice or logo revision can turn into hours of work I can’t bill for.
Do these doubts and checking feel unwanted and intrusive to you?

Yes. I don’t want the thoughts—they just pop back in even after I’ve checked. I’ll know I looked at the mortgage number or the client proof, but then it’s, “What if I missed the one thing that ruins everything?” It feels intrusive and hard to put aside.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive?

Yes. I know it’s more than it should be. I’ll reopen the same files, reread emails, check the payment confirmation again, and repeat the figures in my head until they feel settled. A small invoice or logo change can end up taking hours that I can’t bill for.
When these doubts make you recheck things, do you feel deep down that the fear is probably not reasonable?

Yes, I mean, part of me knows it probably isn’t reasonable. I know I checked the mortgage number or the client proof. But the doubt comes back so strongly—what if I missed the one mistake that costs me everything?—that I can’t seem to let it go.
On a typical day, about how much total time do these checking and mental reviewing rituals take up?

It can take hours altogether. I’ll keep reopening files, rereading emails, checking the payment confirmation, and going over the figures silently until they feel settled. Even a simple invoice or logo revision can eat up hours I can’t bill for.
Do you try to resist the checking or mental reviewing?

I do try to stop myself, but I usually give in to it. I’ll tell myself I’ve checked enough, then reopen the file or look at the payment confirmation again. And I keep repeating the figures in my head until they feel settled.
Outside of the checking episodes, do you generally see yourself as a perfectionistic person who likes things done in a very exact, controlled way?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I like doing good work, but I haven’t thought of myself as someone who needs everything controlled or exact all the time.
Do you get this kind of intense anxiety mainly when other people might judge you or watch what you’re doing?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it being mainly about other people watching or judging me.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different parts of your life, even when you are not caught up in checking something?
I’m not sure I do. Most of the time, it’s really the checking that takes over my thoughts, rather than worrying about lots of different things.
Did these symptoms begin soon after a specific stressful event in your life?
I’m not sure. I can’t think of one specific stressful event that it started right after.
